name: Kneebar Finish
description: Kneebar Finish after Carni requires a separate leg-lock setup. Release the shoulder clamp, then establish hip and ankle control before extending the knee.
conditions: The attacker has isolated one leg between the legs, with the opponent's knee aligned at the hip fulcrum and the ankle controlled.
Confirm control of the opponent's thigh and ankle before considering a knee-extension attack.
Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.
summary: The Kneebar is a straight leg lock that controls the hip and ankle while placing a fulcrum behind the knee, threatening knee extension when the attacker closes the hips.
overview:
The attacker has isolated one leg between the legs, with the opponent's knee aligned at the hip fulcrum and the ankle controlled. Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.

Confirm control of the opponent's thigh and ankle before considering a knee-extension attack. Use the legs to keep the opponent's hip from moving freely away. Place the knee at the hip fulcrum with the leg in a straight, non-twisted line.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Rob Biernacki — three leg-lock control points](https://www.grapplearts.com/three-critical-control-points-leglock/); [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): Which controls bracket the knee before extension is possible?
flashcards.answer: A kneebar requires separate control above and below the knee, including the thigh and ankle.
flashcards.answer_line: The same leg's thigh and ankle

plausible: The same leg's ankle and heel only
Same thigh held but foot left free
trap: One thigh and the opposite ankle

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): What prevents the captured leg's hip from sliding freely away?
flashcards.answer: Use the legs to restrain the hip and thigh so the captured knee does not simply move away from the fulcrum.
flashcards.answer_line: Your legs hold their hip and thigh

plausible: Foot held without thigh contact
Your legs squeeze below their knee
trap: Tight ankle grip with thighs apart

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): Where is the knee positioned in the straight-leg alignment?
flashcards.answer: Align the captured knee at the hip fulcrum in a straight, untwisted leg line.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee at hip fulcrum, leg untwisted

plausible: Knee above hips with thigh sliding
Knee bent around a shin behind it
trap: Knee at hips with foot turned aside

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): How should the ankle be controlled in the straight-leg capture?
flashcards.answer: Hold the lower leg close while preserving alignment; do not turn the foot into a rotational lock.
flashcards.answer_line: Held close with the leg untwisted

plausible: Foot turned out with thigh fixed
Foot free with only knee squeezed
trap: Twist foot inward to straighten leg

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): Where should a cooperative capture drill stop?
flashcards.answer: Practice aligned hip-and-ankle capture without bridging the knee into its end range.

plausible: After a bridge tests backward range
After a foot turn tests rotation
trap: Before ankle grip or thigh capture

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): Which controls release on a tap before either partner turns?
flashcards.answer: Open ankle and thigh control promptly so the whole leg can move before either partner changes direction.
flashcards.answer_line: Both ankle grip and thigh restraint

plausible: Ankle released; thigh still clamped
Thigh released; ankle still held
trap: Only stop extension; keep both grips

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): What geometry identifies a knee-extension threat rather than Carni?
flashcards.answer: The kneebar's separate lower-body capture places the knee at a hip fulcrum and controls the ankle.
flashcards.answer_line: Ankle held, knee aligned at the hips

plausible: Ankle held with knee past your hips
Knee bent around shin, foot tucked

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): Why does the Carni clamp not supply this finishing position?
flashcards.answer: Release the shoulder configuration and separately capture a leg; the sources do not establish a direct Carni-to-kneebar finish.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder captured instead of a leg

plausible: Knee captured but no ankle pressure
Ankle already held; no hip extension
trap: Leg already bracketed; knee too bent

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): A partner starts turning with the ankle fixed; what must you do?
flashcards.answer: Release the captured leg before allowing rotation against a fixed ankle and thigh.
flashcards.answer_line: Free ankle and thigh before turning

plausible: Hold ankle fixed; follow with hips
Open thigh clamp but keep ankle grip
trap: Free ankle but keep thigh pinned

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (attacker): Which loading pattern identifies the intended straight-leg attack?
flashcards.answer: The captured knee lies at the hip fulcrum. The thigh and ankle are controlled on either side, and hip extension would load the knee; stop the cooperative drill before its end range.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee extension, thigh and ankle held

plausible: Knee twist with thigh and foot fixed
Ankle extension over the forearm
trap: Calf squeezed as knee folds on shin

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (defender): Which alignment warns of the straight-leg attack?
flashcards.answer: Recognize the knee at the attacker's hip fulcrum with the ankle controlled as an extension threat.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee at their hips with ankle held

plausible: Knee past their hips with ankle held
Bent knee folded around their shin

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (defender): What do you deny before the lower-leg capture closes?
flashcards.answer: Hand fight early to keep the lower leg free before the attacker completes hip, knee and ankle control.
flashcards.answer_line: A secure grip controlling your ankle

plausible: Only a grip on the other ankle
Only thigh contact; ankle still held
trap: Only their hand outside your hip

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (defender): While the leg is still free, what removes the knee's fulcrum contact?
flashcards.answer: Recover the knee line early while it can move freely; a secured extension lock calls for release rather than a forced escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Move knee off their hip fulcrum

plausible: Move foot sideways with knee fixed
Straight leg with knee at their hips
trap: Pull ankle back with knee line fixed

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (defender): Why avoid turning with your ankle and thigh fixed?
flashcards.answer: Do not twist against a held ankle and trapped thigh; obtain release before changing direction.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee twists between two fixed points

plausible: Ankle follows torso; thigh pinned
Hip restraint blocks all knee twist
trap: Held leg spins without knee rotation

flashcards.question: Kneebar Finish (defender): The knee is securely captured for extension; when should you tap?
flashcards.answer: Tap to the controlled extension threat instead of testing the knee's backward range or waiting for severe pain.

plausible: After hips test backward knee range
Only after added ankle rotation
trap: After one last escape from the lock
